summary: Claim o-6c67371c3798c9dc, anchored to g0029: the old harness cannot reach untriangulated quad export on either source version.

claims.necessity_reason: ParseFromString supports preserving a valid quad as one four-vertex face when triangulate is false. A finite OBJ containing four vertices and one quad can reach that behavior, but the old harness always passes a default configuration with triangulate set to true. Its complete entry has no equivalent route to the four-vertex result.

before.requirement: For a valid quad with config.triangulate=false, retain one face with four vertices.
before.reason: The before source preserves the polygon in the nontriangulating branch. The harness uses only the default configuration, which sets triangulate=true, so a quad takes the two-triangle branch.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The harness-constructed configuration defaults triangulate to true.
ParseFromString forwards that configuration setting to LoadObj.
LoadObj accepts a face with four parsed indices.
LoadObj forwards triangulate to polygon export.

after.requirement: For a valid quad with config.triangulate=false, retain one face with four vertices.
after.reason: The after source retains the same polygon-preserving branch, while the old harness still supplies the true default and cannot select it.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The configuration still defaults triangulate to true.
ParseFromString still forwards that setting to LoadObj.
LoadObj accepts the same four-index face.
LoadObj still forwards triangulate to polygon export.

claims.comparison_reason: The same unchanged default triangulate=true setting blocks the same four-vertex quad result on both sides. Supplying a triangle or a quad that becomes two triangles does not reach that result.
